body: [self-review] PyYAML is unavailable under make unit-test and the gate's python3, and wave 2a's gate must import the hash. fixed:d680a607: a strict front-matter subset parser in the shared module that refuses anything PyYAML would read differently; it matches PyYAML on every accepted task file (validation §6).

[self-review] Six legacy task files start with `---` front matter, three with unquoted timestamps the subset parser refuses; an unparsable legacy header must not become a failure. fixed:d680a607: a parse error counts only when the header claims format 2; test_legacy_files_are_grandfathered covers both cases.

[self-review] The boundary check runs with /usr/bin on PATH in its tests, which is Python 3.9 on macOS. fixed:d680a607: the validator and module avoid 3.10+ APIs (no glob root_dir, no match), checked by running /usr/bin/python3 3.9.6 on the task file.

[self-review] test_word_budgets caps the rule at 450 words (447 before). fixed:d680a607: the invariant is one clause in the Routing bullet, with three meaning-preserving cuts elsewhere, none in a phrase the test pins; 450 words.

[self-review, full suite] test_pr_feedback.test_gate_command_appears_once_in_skill_step_10 pins `BASE=origin/main PR_FEEDBACK_EVIDENCE=<json> make require-crit-review` in step 10, which the first wording broke. fixed:ce9d3dd2: every text writes `make require-crit-review -C <main checkout> REVIEW_TREE=<review worktree>` (GNU make takes -C after the target).

[scope] home/dot_config/codex/AGENTS.md mirrors pr-integration.md and is not in allowed_files; it points to SKILL step 10, which carries the new gate form, so it does not contradict the change. Reported in the report's scope notes for a docs task.
